key_insight: MedUIGym turns clinical GUI workflows into a scalable training and evaluation testbed, revealing persistent agent weaknesses while enabling gains through targeted training.
engineering_relevance: Paired screenshot-based GUI and native-tool interfaces over identical clinical data help engineers evaluate interface-dependent performance and collect training trajectories.
method: Unify 15,739 tasks from 17 benchmark sources across six clinical task families.
Support screenshot perception, mouse-and-keyboard actions, and verification of answers and required clinical actions.
Enable parallel trajectory collection, offline learning, and online reinforcement learning.
evidence_signal: Evaluation of 12 vision-language models found inconsistent gains from increased reasoning effort, while training improved both Qwen3.5 models on in-domain tasks and tasks from external sources.
watch_item: Benchmark improvements do not establish safety or reliability in deployed clinical EHR workflows.
paper_title: MedUIGym: Evaluating and Training GUI Agents for Clinical Workflows
